The headline 'Campaigners build pressure for a nature deal at crunch Geneva talks' keeps the ORIGINAL's subject and most of its wording, just reordered ('Pressure grows for deal to save nature at crunch talks in Geneva') — a cosmetic edit.
The progress line 'Campaigners are mounting pressure on governments to agree a deal to protect nature at the Geneva talks' repeats the headline's claim rather than adding new information.
The progress line's 'The authors of a landmark nature review' makes authorship plural, where the original says a single 'Author of landmark UK review'.

The progress line's 'Trump says the two sides have agreed a partial ceasefire' asserts mutual agreement, but the original shows Zelenskyy disputing it ('news to me'), so it is not established that 'the two sides' agreed anything.

The progress line's claim that the ceasefire covers 'strikes on energy infrastructure' is not stated in the original, which only reports Zelenskyy's earlier, separate rejection of a US call over oil-refinery bombing, not the scope of the announced ceasefire.
The original says Trump 'claims' Kyiv would like to make a deal (a sceptical attribution); the rewrite's trail softens this to neutral 'said', changing the force of the attribution.

The headline 'Trump pushes for immediate Ukraine ceasefire following Zelenskyy meeting' is a thesaurus swap of the original ('calls for'→'pushes for', 'after meeting'→'following... meeting') with the same subject and structure; the copy's actual upside — Kyiv's stated readiness to 'make a deal' — was available to build the headline on instead but is left in the trail.

The rewrite's 'turns away from allies and towards Russia' softens the original's stronger 'turns on allies and embraces Russia' (and the headline's 'tearing up the transatlantic alliance'), weakening the described hostility.

The headline states the €140bn is set to be raised 'for struggling households' as settled fact, when the original only has an official claiming (a hedge, 'says official') that the cap 'will bring solidarity... towards struggling customers' — not that the tax itself is earmarked for households.
The rewrite's trail adds 'the operation to remove a tumour from his lung'; the original only says 'cancer surgery' and 'operation on his lung' and does not mention a tumour being removed.

The original headline states workers are 'facing deadly heat'; the rewrite drops the word 'deadly' throughout (headline and trail both say only 'extreme heat'), weakening the severity of the harm the protections respond to.

The standfirst ('With broader efforts to protect people from extreme heat stalled...') never restates the core harm from the original headline — that US workers are 'facing deadly heat' — so the headline-and-standfirst pair loses the specific danger to workers that rule 5 requires to be stated in full.
